citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I).

citations.quote: According to the results of corrosion experiment, high ratio of NaFSI will continuously corrode electrode and lead to side reactions, and 0.5 M NaFSI showed better resistant to corrosion, so 0.5 M NaFSI, 0.3 M NaFSI and 0.1 M NaFSI were chosen to test the electrochemical performance. The NNFM111/HC full cell was used to test the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte. Referring to the operating voltage range of conventional SIBs, the operating voltage of the batteries was set at 2.0-4.0 V. After filling the electrolyte, the batteries were activated to obtain two important parameters, i.e., impedance and first coulombic efficiency. As presented in table S1 that NaFSI replacing part of the sodium salt not only reduces the impedance of the battery, but also greatly improves the initial coulomb efficiency of the battery. This indicates that the introduction of NaFSI reduces the loss of active sodium during the first charging process, and suppresses the side reaction on the electrode, which explains why the impedance of the battery is also reduced. The cycle performance at room temperature is an important index for SIBs, so the effect of double-salt system on the performance of the NNFM111/HC full cells was evaluated. Compared with the single-salt system, the introduction of NaFSI can improve the discharge capacity of the NNFM111/HC full cell (Figure 4a). As the NaFSI content increases, the cycling life of the NNFM111/HC full cell increased significantly.

citations.quote:
2.1 Electrolyte and pouch cell preparation
Battery grade solvents of propylene carbonate (PC), ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), diethyl carbonate (DEC) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) were obtained from Shenzhen CAPCHEM Technology Co., Ltd, China, and used as received. Sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ , KISHIDA Chemical Co., Ltd, Japan) was dissolved into cold solvent mixtures with different volume ratios. Water contents of all resultant electrolytes were determined by the Karl Fischer titration to be lower than $15~\mathrm{ppm}$ .

The $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathode material was scale-up synthesized as described previously [17]. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode were prepared by coating slurries consisting of 92 wt.% active material, 4 wt.% super P, and 4 wt.% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) in N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) onto an aluminum foil, respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were stacked and packaged into a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. After heating at 80 °C for 48 h under vacuum, the dried pouch cells were moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte.

citations.quote:
Abstract
Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

Keywords: Sodium-ion battery; $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ ; thermal stability; nonaqueous electrolyte; safety; Engineering optimization

citations.quote: Adopting the concept of using more comprehensive performance reflecting by pouch cells for experimental work, undoubtedly can make the researches have better academic and commercial value. Bases on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group in TDFP molecular, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is firstly developed to enhance the drastic temperature performance of pouch NFM/HC cells. This TDFP-containing electrolyte can realize a “formation-repair” film-formation aim and form tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes. Different from NaDFP, TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich SEI/CEI but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition. Most importantly, it can pre-form a film on the electrode surface without charging, thus suppressing of solvent decomposition participation in film formation during charging. As results, the cycling and storage stability of pouch NFM/HC cells are considerably improved over a wide-temperature from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ .

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), sodium hexafluorophosphate $\left(\mathrm{NaPF}_{6}\right)$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TDFP were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the HC anode. The areal loadings of the anode were 16.0 g $m^{-2}$ and 1.6 g $cm^{-3}$ . The areal loadings of the cathode were 33.0 g $m^{-2}$ , and 3.4 g $cm^{-3}$ . The injection amount of electrolyte of pouch cell was 3.0 g $Ah^{-1}$ , the designed capacity of single pouch cell was 1 Ah. The semi-finished pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.

Furthermore, performance tests were conducted at even lower temperatures, and it was found that the cells with TDFP still maintained an 86% discharge capacity retention rate at -30 °C. Low temperature cycling test is followed to further validate the superior performance of TDFP. As illustrated in Fig. 4d, the cell with TDFP exhibited the best cycling stability, followed by TMSP, then NaDFP, and finally the Baseline. It is worth noting that the performance of TMSP and NaDFP batteries under low-temperature cycling was the reverse of that under room-temperature cycling. This suggests that the failure mechanisms of the batteries and the reasons for performance enhancement by additives also differ. The thicknesses of cells haven't visible change before and after cycling, meaning no significant gas generation could be observed under low-temperature conditions (Fig. 4e). This contrasts with the results under room-temperature cycling, leading to the slightly better performance of TMSP-containing cells compared to NaDFP-containing cells under low-temperature conditions.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec1::child2
citations.quote: Schematic diagram of the mechanism of electrolytes with low-temperature adaptive solvation structure. Herein, we construct a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte with a low salt concentration. Specifically, 1,3-dioxolane (DOL) as an ultraweak solvent is mixed into 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ diglyme (G2) electrolyte. This electrolyte can form an anion-enhanced and solvent-weakened solvation structure at LT, as shown in Figure 1. The dipole-dipole interaction between DOL and G2 reduces the electronegativity of the oxygen in G2 and weakening the ion-dipole interaction of Na $^{+}$ -O (G2). Thus, as the temperature drops from room temperature to low temperature, this leads to more anions and less G2 molecules involved in primary solvation shell of Na $^{+}$ . This accelerates transport of Na $^{+}$ and induces the formation of uniform and continuous solid electrolyte interface (SEI) on HC at LT. This results in lower voltage polarization on the surface of HC and leveraging the plateau capacity of HC. This strikingly facilitates HC-based SIBs to have higher capacity and more stable cycling performance at LT.

To test the practical application of electrolytes, a piece pouch cell (45 mAh) was assembled for cycling testing in Figure 6d and Figure S26 (Supporting Information). Therefore, 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL electrolyte with a temperature-adaptive solvent structure holds great potential in the practical application of SIBs. Additionally, the temperature-adapted solvation structure may widespreadly exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes. We have tested the low-temperature performance of G2/THF, DME/DOL and DME/THF based electrolytes, as shown in Figure S27 (Supporting Information). citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec6::child0
citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec0::child0
citations.quote:
Yuewei Cui, Youxuan Ni, Yuankun Wang, Linyue Wang, Wenxuan Yang, Shuang Wu, Weiwei Xie, Kai Zhang, Zhenhua Yan,\* and Jun Chen\*

Sodium-ion batteries are applied to cold-resistant energy storage hindered by phase transitions and sluggish $Na^{+}$ migration of traditional carbonate-based electrolytes at low temperatures. The desolvation of $Na^{+}$ is a crucial step in impeding the transport of $Na^{+}$ , which primarily attributes to the robust solvent coordination of $Na^{+}$ . Herein, a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte with an ultraweakly coordinated 1,3-dioxolane (DOL) is designed for constructing anion-rich solvation structure in a diglyme (G2)-based electrolyte. The electronegativity of the oxygen atoms of G2 is attenuated by dipole-dipole interaction between DOL and G2. As the temperature drops, the weakened $Na^{+}-O$ (G2) interaction leads to increased anionic coordination and less solvent coordination, facilitating the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ . This anionic-enhanced solvation structure contributes to the formation of stable solid electrolyte interface at the hard carbon (HC) anode, which accelerates $Na^{+}$ transport and diminishing the voltage polarization at low temperatures. Consequently, the HC anode can retain a high capacity of 203.9 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -50 °C, and the pouch cell composed of $HC||Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ at -30 °C achieves a capacity retention of 92.43% after 100 cycles at 0.1 C.

citations.quote: Electrolyte design strategies are closely related to the capacities, cycle life and safety of sodium-ion batteries. In this study, we are aimed to optimize electrolyte with the focus on engineering aspects. The basic physicochemical properties including ionic conductivity, viscosity, wettability and thermochemical stability of the electrolytes using $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ as the solute and the mixed solvent with different components of EMC, DMC or DEC in PC or EC were systematically measured. Ah pouch cell with $\mathrm{NaNi}_{1/3}\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1/3}\mathrm{O}_2/$ hard carbon electrodes was used to evaluate the performance of the prepared electrolytes. By using the Inductive Coupled Plasma Emission Spectrometer (ICP), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC) and Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC), we show that an optimized electrolyte can effectively promote the formation of a protective interfacial layer on two electrodes, which not only retards parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte but also suppresses dissolution of metal ions from the cathode. With an optimized electrolyte, a $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon cell can attain 56.16% capacity retention under the low temperature of -40 °C, and can be able to retain 80% capacity retention after more than 2500 cycles while presenting excellent thermal safety.

citations.quote:
2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were first prepared, and then stacked with 10 cathode electrodes by 11 anode electrodes and packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.

citations.chunk_id: 0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec2::child0
citations.quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.quote: In summary, NaDFP is introduced as a dual-functional additive for pouch SIBs to achieve high electrochemical performance within a wide temperature range ( $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). There are two ways to improve the battery performance for NaDFP: i) induce high-quality CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces; ii) optimize the solvation structure to decrease the desolvation energy and surface impendence. Consequently, its role in other types of commercial electrolytes was further investigated. NaDFP electrolyte demonstrates the potential application in wide temperature SIBs from $-30$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Importantly, only 1 wt% addition of NaDFP into electrolyte can enable considerably effective improvement, which is essential to reduce the cost of batteries. Therefore, this work provides a new idea for the optimum design of electrolytes of SIBs and other energy storage equipment.

CONCLUSIONS
NaBOB dissolved in NMP, TMP, or their mixtures provide promising electrolytes for sodium-ion battery research. The proposed electrolytes outperform many previously studied electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries in terms of ionic conductivity, high-temperature performance, and having the potential to decrease the electrolyte cost. The studied electrolytes provided promising long-term cycling in full-cell sodium-ion batteries based on hard carbon anodes and Prussian white cathodes. NaBOB–NMP–TMP electrolytes containing less than 30 vol % NMP are nonflammable and share properties like good ionic conductivity over a wide temperature range while possessing good high-temperature performance and retaining over 50% capacity over 1000 cycles.

citations.quote: To map the NMP–TMP solvent system, eleven samples were first prepared ranging from NMP to TMP as the sole solvents with 10 vol % increments to prepare the binary solvent mixtures. These mixtures are here denoted as X:Y where X represents the vol% of NMP and Y indicates the vol % of TMP (see Figure 1a). We found that the two solvents are fully miscible and that they produced a clear homogeneous liquid. Pure TMP can dissolve up to 0.42 M (7.2 wt %) NaBOB, while pure NMP was close to saturation at 0.66 M (12.8 wt %) NaBOB. For the intermediate samples, there was a clear correlation between increased solubility and NMP content. The solubility presented herein was achieved by simple stirring, and we recognize that higher concentrations of the salt are probably feasible if heating and long-time scales are used for the dissolution of the salt. The conductivity of the whole series was measured as a function of NaBOB concentration at room temperature (see Figure 1b). The results show that both NMP and TMP as well as the solvent mixtures all achieve their maximum conductivity at their maximum concentration. NaBOB-TMP reached $4.5\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , while NaBOB-NMP attained $8.83\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ , which is higher than the ionic conductivity of the "standard" electrolyte 1 M $\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ in EC:DEC that is reported to reach $6.44\mathrm{mS}\cdot \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ .

Since a battery electrolyte must possess a good balance of many different properties, the conclusion is that NMP addition to TMP can improve conductivity and lower freezing point but any addition above 10 vol % will introduce detrimental effects. papers: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Developing high-safety electrolytes with wide-temperature applicability is a key challenge in advancing the practical application of sodium-ion batteries. In this work, we present a rational electrolyte design strategy that constructs an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free electrolyte based on a carbonate-phosphate mixed solvent system, achieving a balance among cost-effectiveness, sustainability, safety, and temperature tolerance. The relatively weak coordination ability of ethyl methyl carbonate facilitates a favorable reorganization of solvation chemistry at conventional concentrations, promoting greater incorporation of anions and additives into the primary $Na^{+}$ solvation sheath. This leads to the preferential formation of a robust electrode-electrolyte interphase, effectively resolving the persistent issue of phosphate solvent decomposition at the anode interface. Moreover, the designed electrolyte features intrinsic nonflammability, low viscosity, high ionic conductivity, and rapid interfacial kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. More importantly, both Ah-level pouch cells and 18,650 cylindrical cells exhibit superior electrochemical performance, strongly validating the considerable industrial potential of this electrolyte design strategy.

citations.chunk_id: 0364_Zhou 等 - 2026 - A nonflammable carbonate-phosphate hybrid electrolyte enabling high-temperature sodium-ion full batt::sec3::child2
citations.quote: Furthermore, the application of phosphate-based electrolytes in high-temperature SIBs has rarely been reported. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a low-cost and environmentally friendly strategy for regulating the solvation structure, capable of constructing a stable EEI without relying on fluorine-containing components, thereby facilitating the practical application of phosphate-based electrolytes and ensuring the safe and stable operation of SIBs at elevated temperatures. In this work, we developed an intrinsically nonflammable and fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs by employing conventional carbonate cosolvents, ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC). The introduction of EMC modulates the ion-dipole interactions, leading to the formation of a multi-component synergistic solvation structure. This unique solvation structure facilitates the derivation of a stable EEI on both the cathode and anode, effectively suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition and transition metal dissolution. Furthermore, the addition of EMC significantly reduces the viscosity and desolvation energy of the electrolyte system, thereby enhancing ion transport kinetics. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell exhibits excellent temperature adaptability from 10 °C to 100 °C, and remains a high capacity of 79.6% after 400 cycles in 18,650 cylindrical cells.

2.1. Electrolyte design
Although phosphate-based electrolytes possess intrinsic high safety, their practical application faces two major challenges (Fig. 1a): (i) Poor compatibility with electrode materials, which is attributed to the strong coordination ability of phosphate molecules that induces the phosphate-dominated solvation structure [19]. This leads to the unstable EEI with continuous electrolyte decomposition and severe capacity degradation, which aggravates at elevated temperatures. (ii) Inherently high viscosity, which limits ion transport and rate capability [26]. To address these issues, this work introduces a cosolvent with weak coordination ability and low viscosity, aiming to modulate the ion-dipole interactions within the phosphate ester-based electrolyte and optimize its physicochemical properties. The resulting multi-component synergistic solvation structure is expected to facilitate the formation of a stable EEI, thereby fundamentally improving electrolyte-electrode compatibility and enabling the practical application of phosphate ester-based electrolytes in high-safety SIBs. Meanwhile, $NaClO_{4}$ is selected due to its greater commercial maturity compared to high-cost fluorinated salts (such as NaFSI and NaTFSI), offering significant cost effectiveness for large-scale popularization. Although the strong oxidizing nature of $NaClO_{4}$ introduces certain safety concerns, pairing it with intrinsically non-flammable phosphate-based solvents and strictly implementing safety operation procedures can effectively mitigate potential safety risks.

To further evaluate the practical relevance of NTE electrolyte, PB|| HC full cells with high-mass loading electrodes are assembled (Fig. 4a). Full cells with NTE electrolyte significantly outperform their NT counterpart, with a higher capacity of 126.8 vs. $105.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , a superior initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of $82.0\%$ vs. $69.5\%$ , and better capacity retention of $81.2\%$ vs. $76.0\%$ after 200 cycles (Fig. 4b and c). As shown in Figs. 4d and S12, the NTE electrolyte enables markedly enhanced rate performance. The full cell delivers a high capacity of $128.9\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ , substantially exceeding the $97.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ achieved with the NT electrolyte. This advantage is maintained at a high rate of $1.5\mathrm{C}$ , where the NTE-based cell retains $69.2\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , in contrast to only $42.5\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ for the NT-based cell. When systematically compared in Fig. 4e, the NTE system exhibits significantly higher capacity retention across all tested current rates. The smaller polarization observed across various rates can be attributed to the formation of robust CEI/SEI layers and reduced desolvation energy in the NTE system.

These findings underscore the enhanced interfacial stability and energy retention of NTE, playing great potential on large-scale energy storage system.

citations.quote: The temperature tolerance of NTE electrolyte is further evaluated in sodium-ion full cell. As shown in Fig. 5a, PB||HC cells employing NTE maintain stable charge-discharge performance over a temperature range from 10 °C to 100 °C. Additionally, the cell with NTE achieves superior cycling performance at 55 °C, maintaining a high capacity of 100.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. This performance is significantly higher than that of the NT-based cell, which delivers only 72.4 mAh g $^{-1}$ under identical conditions (Figs. 5b and S17). Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial kinetics, the full cell with NTE electrolyte delivers excellent rate performance from 0.1 C to 1.5 C at 55 °C (Figs. 5c and S18). It maintains a reversible capacity of 96.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 1.5 C, corresponding to 79.7% capacity at 0.1 C. While rapid capacity degradation at high rates with large polarization is observed in full cell with NT electrolyte, indicating its inferior compatibility within the full-cell system (Fig. 5d). In addition, the self-discharge test indicates that full cell with NTE electrolyte demonstrates superior ICE of 85.4% and reduced potential drop of 362.6 mV at 55 °C, compared to 74.2% and 398.4 mV with NT electrolyte (Fig. S19). As presented in Fig. 5e, the cylindrical cell using NTE electrolyte demonstrates a reversible capacity of 743.8 mAh after 50 cycles at 55 °C, corresponding to the high capacity retention of 93.0%.

citations.chunk_id: 0084_Zhang 等 - 2026 - Rational solvation structure tuning via cosolvent engineering for nonflammable and wide-temperature::sec3::child2
citations.quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

citations.chunk_id: 0084_Zhang 等 - 2026 - Rational solvation structure tuning via cosolvent engineering for nonflammable and wide-temperature::sec4::child1
citations.quote: This strategy achieves synergistic optimization of wide-temperature performance, cost efficiency, and environmental sustainability while preserves the intrinsic safety advantages of phosphate-based electrolytes, providing a practical solution for developing safe and wide-temperature sodium-ion full batteries. Based on the frontier molecular orbital theory, the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy level of molecules, corresponding to the oxidation and reduction thermodynamic potentials [43], are calculated in Fig. 1b. Compared with the commonly used ether solvents, TEP endows the lower HOMO energy level, indicating its excellent antioxidant ability; however, it tends to preferentially decompose at anode surface due to its much lower LUMO energy level, forming the unstable TEP-based solid electrolyte interface (SEI). Moreover, the charge densities of atoms are simulated by electrostatic potential (ESP) density distributions in Fig. 1c, where electrophilic sites mainly concentrated on oxygen atoms and nucleophilic sites on hydrogen atoms [31]. In this work, G2 is introduced as cosolvent into phosphate-based electrolyte to investigate its effects on the solvation structure and interfacial properties. $\mathrm{NaClO_4}$ , known for its low cost, low moisture sensitivity, and fluorine-free nature, was selected as the electrolyte salt.

citations.quote: Herein, we innovatively employ G2 (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether) cosolvent, which exhibits excellent compatibility with hard carbon anodes, to modulate the solvation structure of triethyl phosphonate (TEP)-based electrolyte, successfully developing a fully fluorine-free, flame-retardant electrolyte characterized by low cost, high safety, wide temperature and environmental friendliness. The G2-dominated solvation structure enables the synchronous construction of stable EEI at the surface of both cathode and anode, thereby significantly suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition, mitigating transition metal dissolution and inhibiting structural degradation of electrode materials. Benefiting from the robust EEI, the Prussian blue||hard carbon (PB||HC) full cell demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance at a wide temperature range from 25 to 55 °C. Furthermore, validation experiments employing PB||HC pouch cells and layered oxide||HC full cells further confirm the broad applicability and industrial potential of this electrolyte system in practical applications. The fully fluorine-free phosphate-based electrolytes design strategy proposed in this study not only achieves synergistic optimization of critical parameters including wide-temperature performance, manufacturing cost, safety and environmental sustainability, but also provides essential theoretical insights and technical support for developing next-generation sodium-ion full batteries.

citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for development of all-climate carbonate electrolyte and it offers the straight approach to high-performance commercial pouch SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec10::child0
citations.quote: In summary, “hard-soft synergy” strategy—reasonably coupling NaDFP with TMSP or TMSB as the functional electrolytes successfully achieved wide-temperature performance of pouch SIBs over a range of $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Benefit to the high-quality and rich element optimized NaDFP-based CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces, and optimizing electrolyte structure which decrease the desolvation energy and induce superior electrolyte properties, a high capacity retention of $92\%$ after 350 cycles and a stable cycling performance at $1\mathrm{C}$ were achieved even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Besides, both the discharge capacity at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ were also greatly improved. Importantly, only tiny dose of NaDFP, TMSB/TMSP with reasonably couple could enable considerably effective performance improvement of SIBs, which is essential to reduce the cost and advance the commercialization. This work not only obtains functional electrolytes for enhanced wide-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs, but also sheds lights on the designing multi-functional additive electrolytes of SIBs.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

2.2 Battery Assembly
$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . citations.quote: To solve this problem, a CIE was designed in this work. The design principle is based on the following findings: there are always some solvents in the electrolyte that do not participate in the coordination and only act as ion transport media, which are called free solvents. For this reason, we replaced this part of free solvent with 2-methyloxolane (MO) which has a lower melting point ( $-136^{\circ}C$ , Table S1) and is less polar. Through this strategy, not only the co-embeddable solvation structure is retained and the ion transport kinetics are accelerated, but also the working temperature range of electrolyte in low-temperature environment is significantly widened by increasing the solvation entropy. To highlight the progressiveness of our designed electrolyte, we also used common co-intercalation ether electrolyte (CCE) and WSE as controls, and the specific electrolyte formulation is shown in Table S2. According to the optical photographs in Figure S1, CCE starts to have salt precipitation at $-30^{\circ}C$ , and it is even completely solidified at $-50^{\circ}C$ . On the other hand, WSE and our CIE remain liquid at $-50^{\circ}C$ , which effectively guarantees the possibility of electrolyte application at low temperatures. The ion transport mechanisms of various electrolytes at low temperatures are shown in Fig. 1, among which the CIE has the fastest ion transport rate due to the presence of the co-intercalation behavior.

citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

citations.quote: $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ additive was incorporated in the pouch cell composed of the hard carbon/O3-type positive electrode and evaluated (Fig. 4a). The addition of the $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ salt in the electrolyte improved capacity retention considerably compared with that of the typical FEC-added electrolyte. While the FEC-added pouch cell exhibited a capacity retention of $73.1\%$ at the 400th cycle, the addition of $\mathrm{LiPF_6}$ salt in the SIB electrolyte demonstrated a capacity retention of $92.7\%$ at the same cycle number. This achieved capacity retention is highly surpasses previously reported results, which is typically about $80\%$ (Table S1). The working nominal voltage change during the cycle indicates that the development of polarization from side reactions occurred in the case of the FEC-added cell (Fig. 4b). The working voltage with the $LiPF_{6}$ -added electrolyte was highly preserved in different cycles, implying that the energy delivered from the addition of the $LiPF_{6}$ pouch cell was well retained after the 400th cycle. Figure 4b demonstrates the cycle number-dependent voltage profiles obtained from hard carbon/O3-type positive electrode pouch cells. While polarization increased during repeated cycling in the FEC-added cell case, the $LiPF_{6}$ -added cell showed a stable voltage profile even after the 400th cycle.

citations.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0
citations.quote: Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5. The cells were galvanostatic charged/discharged with a LAND 2001 CT battery test system (Wuhan, China) under various voltage ranges and current rates. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out on a VMP system (Biologic S.A., Claix, France).

Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5. The cells were galvanostatic charged/discharged with a LAND 2001 CT battery test system (Wuhan, China) under various voltage ranges and current rates. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out on a VMP system (Biologic S.A., Claix, France).

citations.quote: One may still argue the accuracy of in situ XRD tests as the signal of metallic Na would not be detectable until the amount is accumulated to a specific value. In order to determine the Na plating capacity more punctually, ex situ XRD is conducted on HC electrodes in coin cells with capacity limitation from 200 to $300\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ . The cells were cycled for 10 cycles to accumulate potential metallic Na. XRD patterns were collected at a discharged state. As shown in Figure S4, no Na peak is observed beneath the capacity of $250\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ , and the Na signal appeared in $300\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ sample. The Coulombic efficiency provides implications. The average Coulombic efficiency is around $97.4\%$ for the cells cycling at a limited capacity of $250\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ or less. The value is close to $97.8\%$ when the cell is tested at room temperature with a cut-off voltage of 0 V. For the cell cycled at $300\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ , the Coulombic efficiency decreases to only $95.3\%$ due to the Na plating/stripping.

citations.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child16
citations.quote: The voltage profiles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell consists of a plateau at 4.1 V and sloping regime between 3.6-2.5 V, contributing to an accumulative capacity of 306 mAh g $^{-1}$ (based on the mass of anode). The energy density is calculated to be 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ based on the total weight of cathode and anode, along with an average discharge potential of 3.62 V. A stable cyclic performance similar to that in half-cell is achieved at $25^{\circ}$ C, as indicated by full cell F1 in Figure 5b. Ulteriorly, we tested the behavior of full cell under low temperature. Firstly, the performance of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ half-cell at 0°C and -20°C are measured and given in Figure S7a and S7b. The reversible capacity decreases with lowering the temperature. It maintains 93.2% and 80.4% of the capacity at room temperature for testing at 0°C and -20°C, respectively. Nevertheless, cyclic stability is kept. It is worthwhile to mention that the safe capacity for HC working at -20°C is 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ , which is also around 80% of its capacity at room temperature. Therefore, there is no need to change the mass ratio of the cathode and anode in the full cell for operating at low temperature.

citations.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child17
citations.quote: Therefore, there is no need to change the mass ratio of the cathode and anode in the full cell for operating at low temperature. As expected, the $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell also demonstrates a capacity reduction at 0 °C in the first several cycles and reaches stable capacity retention of 244 mAh g $^{-1}$ (F2 in Figure 5b). However, when the full cell was charged/discharged at -20°C, a significant drop in capacity is observed, particularly during the first 5 cycles. It may lie in the increased resistance on the anode side as reflected by EIS. The dynamic property of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ at different temperatures is also evaluated using galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT), as indicated in Figure 5c. From the calculation, the diffusion coefficient of Na-ions ( $D_{Na}^{+}$ ) at 25°C is in the range of $10^{-9}$ to $10^{-10}$ cm $^{2}$ s $^{-1}$ . The value is only slightly decreased at 0°C. In sharp contrast, the $D_{Na}^{+}$ value is about one magnitude lower at -25 °C than that at 25°C. The slow $Na^{+}$ diffusion is in agreement with the EIS results that the thicker SEI film would affect the ion diffusion. After testing at $-20^{\circ}C$ for 10 cycles, the same cell (F3) was put back to $25^{\circ}C$ and its capacity gradually recovered and regained ca. 82% of the capacity at $25^{\circ}C$ .

citations.quote: In summary, a hard carbon material for NIBs is fabricated from low-cost biomass waste using a facile two-step thermal treatment. Compared to direct high-temperature carbonization, the pre-treatment at a medium temperature is beneficial to avoiding the selfactivation effect of impurities. An appropriate surface area and pore size distribution are obtained, enabling a stable capacity of around 300 mAh g $^{-1}$ . It also shows excellent performance at a temperature as low as -20 °C. A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C, as evidenced by in situ XRD and Raman tests. As-prepared HC also delivers stable performance in the full cell coupling with a $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ cathode, demonstrated an energy density of 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ (based on the total weight of electrode) with decent cyclic stability at room temperature. Nevertheless, the full cell shows a fast capacity fading at -20 °C due to both the increased resistance and continuous consumption of Na ions. It calls for building stable SEI under low temperature in future studies.

The sodium ion diffusion coefficients of NVPF/CNTs at room temperature and $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ are both reached $10^{-12}\mathrm{cm}^2\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ . This is the reason why NVPF/CNTs has good electrochemical performance at low temperature. Besides, to verify the feasibility of NVPF/CNTs in practical application, we assembled full cells using NVPF/CNTs cathode and hard carbon anode (HC). Before the full cells assembling, HC anodes were chemically pre-sodiated at $100 \, mA \, g^{-1}$ to reduce the irreversibility and enhance the stability of the full cell during cycling [63]. citations.quote: Figure 1a and Table S1 (Supporting Information) present the temperature-dependent ionic conductivities of the dilute NaPF $_{6}$ -based ether electrolyte (0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ in DEGDME, 0.5-P-D), the conventional concentration NaPF $_{6}$ -based ether electrolyte (1.0 M NaPF $_{6}$ in DEGDME, 1.0-P-D), and the commercial ester-based electrolyte (1.0 M NaPF $_{6}$ in the mixture of ethylene carbonate (EC) and dimethyl carbonate (DMC) with a volume ratio of 1:1, 1.0-P-E/M). At 25 °C, 0.5-P-D exhibits a lower ionic conductivity (2.7 mS cm $^{-1}$ ) compared to 1.0-P-D (7.3 mS cm $^{-1}$ ) and 1.0-P-E/M (15.3 mS cm $^{-1}$ ) due to its low salt concentration. Over the temperature range from 25 to -50 °C, all three electrolytes display a negative correlation between ionic conductivity and temperature. However, the higher freezing points (Figure S1, Supporting Information) and steep increase in viscosity at low temperatures (Figures S2 and S3, Supporting Information) lead to decreased fluidity and even solidification of the 1.0-P-D and 1.0-P-E/M electrolytes, resulting in a sharp decline in ionic conductivity below 0 °C. In contrast, 0.5-P-D still exhibits a high value of 0.45 mS cm $^{-1}$ even at -50 °C, enabling considerable Na $^{+}$ migration in the liquid electrolyte at low temperatures. The coordination environments in the 0.5-P-D, 1.0-P-D, and 1.0-P-E/M electrolytes were characterized by Raman spectroscopy (Figure 1b).

citations.quote:
In the dilute diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) electrolyte, DEGDME molecules are demonstrated to be highly involved in solvation structure, playing a crucial role in reducing the $Na^{+}$ desolvation energy barrier while preferentially adsorbing on the hard carbon (HC) anode surface. This results in the formation of a $NaF/Na_{2}CO_{3}$ -rich heterostructured SEI, offering additional $Na^{+}$ transport pathways through the $Na_{2}CO_{3}$ and along the $NaF/Na_{2}CO_{3}$ interface. The constructed heterostructured SEI exhibits significantly facilitated $Na^{+}$ diffusion kinetics, a high Young's modulus, and excellent mechanical stability. As a result, HC anode with this dilute electrolyte achieves a high specific capacity of

238 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -40 °C and demonstrates excellent cycling stability at -20 °C, with a capacity retention of 89.67% after 1800 cycles at 1 C. Moreover, the $Na_{0.85}Li_{0.12}Ni_{0.22}Mn_{0.66}O_{2}||HC$ full cells retain 85% of the room-temperature capacity when operating at -20 °C.

citations.quote: The cell applying 1.0-P-D electrolyte exhibits a specific capacity of 236 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -20 °C, which decreases to 202 mAh g $^{-1}$ (only 75.37% capacity retention of room temperature) at -40 °C (Figure S11, Supporting Information). In contrast, the cells employing 0.5-P-D demonstrate a high reversible specific capacity of 251 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -20 °C and 238 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -40 °C (86.86% capacity retention of room temperature), respectively. This superior performance can be attributed to the favorable physicochemical properties and rapid Na $^{+}$ transport kinetics of the 0.5-P-D electrolyte at low temperatures, outperforming previously reported low-temperature electrolytes for SIBs (Table S3, Supporting Information). Figure 2b presents the cycling performance of HC||Na cells at 1 C and -20 °C. The HC||Na cell with 1.0-P-E/M is barely operatable, while the HC anode delivers a specific capacity of $\approx150\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ in 1.0-P-D. However, the cell with 1.0-P-D showcases instability during charge/discharge processes, culminating in failure after 30 cycles. Conversely, the HC||Na cell employing 0.5-P-D electrolyte exhibits a high specific capacity of $\sim210\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ , with a capacity retention of 89.67% after 1800 cycles at 1 C (Figure S12, Supporting Information).

citations.chunk_id: 0013_Deng 等 - 2025 - Heterostructured Solid Electrolyte Interphase Enables Facilitated Kinetics for Low-Temperature Sodiu::sec3::child3
citations.quote: Each cell using these electrolytes delivers a specific capacity of ≈100 mAh g $^{-1}$ at room temperature. However, the full cells employing 1.0-P-E/M or 1.0-P-D exhibit rapid deterioration as temperature decreases. In contrast, the cell with 0.5-P-D maintains a high specific capacity of 85 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -20 °C (85% of the room temperature capacity) and 56 mAh g $^{-1}$ even under -40 °C (Figure S16, Supporting Information). Furthermore, the cycling stability of the three electrolytes at -20 °C was investigated (Figure 2e). The capacity of NLNMO||HC full cells with 1.0-P-E/M and 1.0-P-D exhibits a rapid decay until failure, whereas 0.5-P-D demonstrates a capacity retention of up to 89.65% after 50 cycles at 0.1 C. To investigate the interfacial kinetics, the Tafel curves of the HC||HC symmetric cells in different electrolytes were employed to assess the exchange current density ( $J_0$ ). The results suggest the $J_0$ of 0.5-P-D (0.017 mA cm $^{-2}$ ) is much higher than those of 1.0-P-D (0.009 mA cm $^{-2}$ ) and 1.0-P-E-M (0.004 mA cm $^{-2}$ ), indicating the facilitated kinetics in 0.5-P-D (Figure 2f). Moreover, temperature-dependent electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was conducted to further investigate the interfacial kinetics (Figure S17 and Tables S4–S6, Supporting Information).

citations.chunk_id: 0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec7::child0
citations.quote: The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode.

citations.quote: To solve this problem, a CIE was designed in this work. The design principle is based on the following findings: there are always some solvents in the electrolyte that do not participate in the coordination and only act as ion transport media, which are called free solvents. For this reason, we replaced this part of free solvent with 2-methyloxolane (MO) which has a lower melting point ( $-136^{\circ}C$ , Table S1) and is less polar. Through this strategy, not only the co-embeddable solvation structure is retained and the ion transport kinetics are accelerated, but also the working temperature range of electrolyte in low-temperature environment is significantly widened by increasing the solvation entropy. To highlight the progressiveness of our designed electrolyte, we also used common co-intercalation ether electrolyte (CCE) and WSE as controls, and the specific electrolyte formulation is shown in Table S2. According to the optical photographs in Figure S1, CCE starts to have salt precipitation at $-30^{\circ}C$ , and it is even completely solidified at $-50^{\circ}C$ . On the other hand, WSE and our CIE remain liquid at $-50^{\circ}C$ , which effectively guarantees the possibility of electrolyte application at low temperatures. The ion transport mechanisms of various electrolytes at low temperatures are shown in Fig. 1, among which the CIE has the fastest ion transport rate due to the presence of the co-intercalation behavior.

citations.chunk_id: 0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec6::child0
citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.chunk_id: 0033_Li 等 - 2026 - Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level po::sec1::child0
citations.quote:
Received: 17 June 2025

Accepted: 23 January 2026

Published online: 06 February 2026

Meng Li $^{1}$ , Zeping Liu $^{1}$ , Yu Zhao $^{1}$ , Zhaoyu Chen $^{2}$ , Yu Zhang $^{3}$ & Naiqing Zhang $^{1}$

Check for updates

Sodium ion batteries are attracting extensive interest due to their low cost and abundant sodium resources. However, sodium ion batteries still suffer from severe performance degradation at low temperatures due to the conflict between ion desolvation and diffusion. Herein, we design a co-intercalation ether electrolyte to achieve solvent co-intercalation in the hard carbon negative electrode, thereby bypassing the slow desolvation process while ensuring rapid ion diffusion in electrolyte and hard carbon. The optimized solvation structure also promotes the formation of a thin, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interface, facilitating interfacial ion transport. As a result, the co-intercalation electrolyte enables hard carbon to deliver good low-temperature performance, with an initial Coulombic efficiency of 80.5% at $-50^{\circ}C$ (20 mA g $^{-1}$ ) and a capacity retention of 93% after 200 cycles (100 mA g $^{-1}$ ). Moreover, an Ah-level full cell retains cell stack-level (excluding packaging) specific energy of 163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ at 25 °C and 107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ at $-50^{\circ}C$ (100 mA g $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating the practical feasibility of this strategy for wide-temperature sodium ion batteries.

reviews.reason: The candidate (1 M NaDFOB in DEGDME) is the paper's own electrolyte, directly supported for low-temperature sodium full cells with a hard-carbon anode and shown compatible with NVPF-type cathodes, so the electrolyte selection is recommended. However, the central no-plating capacity limit at -20 °C and the exact NVPF||HC full cell are not established, so the overall goal is not fully addressed.
reviews.association: The NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte is the exact subject of the paper: the authors choose 1 M NaDFOB-G2, test NFPP electrodes at -20/-40 °C, assemble HC//NFPP full and Ah-level pouch cells tested at -20 to 60 °C, and separately show Na3V2(PO4)2F3 (NVPF) electrodes cycle stably with this electrolyte. Together these connect the candidate electrolyte to a low-temperature Na full cell with a hard-carbon anode and to NVPF compatibility; however, the exact NVPF||HC full cell and any no-plating capacity limit were not experimentally measured.

citations.quote:
Miaomiao Xia, Hui Chen, Zhenxu Zheng, Qingfei Meng, $^{*}$ Along Zhao, Xiaoyang Chen, Xinping Ai, Yongjin Fang, $^{*}$ and Yuliang Cao $^{*}$

Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising alternative for next-generation energy storage solutions, driven by the economic and environmental benefits of abundant sodium resources. A pivotal aspect of SIB advancement is the development of advanced electrolytes, which remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a facile and scalable synthesis method for low-cost sodium-difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) is reported and explored its application as a standalone electrolyte salt for SIBs. The NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, solvent compatibility, and the unique capacity to form a dense, robust solid-electrolyte interphase layer on electrode surfaces. As a result, the $\mathrm{Na_{4}Fe_{3}(PO_{4})_{2}P_{2}O_{7}}$ (NFPP) cathode with NaDFOB-based electrolyte exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability with a remarkable capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles. Furthermore, an Ah-level hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell using NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte shows an impressive cycle life of 500 cycles, coupled with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%. The pouch cells also maintain superior electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range from -40 to 60 °C, showcasing the electrolyte's versatility.

The electrolytes with different concentrations of NaDFOB in G2 were prepared, which allows for concentrations greater than 2 M (Figure S1, Supporting Information). According to the conductivity-concentration curve (Figure 1d), the conductivity of the electrolytes increases with increasing concentration. Impressively, the conductivity of the electrolyte reaches up to 6.8 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 1 M and achieves the highest value of 7.94 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 1.4 M. To make a better contrast with conventional electrolytes, the 1 M NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte was chosen for subsequent characterization. The ionic conductivity of 1 M NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte at different temperatures was tested. With the decrease in temperature, the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte gradually reduces (Figure 1e). Notably, the ionic conductivity of NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte still maintains 0.99 mS cm $^{-1}$ at -40 °C, much higher than that of the 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -G2 (0.27 mS cm $^{-1}$ , Figure S2, Supporting Information). The oxidation potential of the NaDFOB-G2 electrolyte was measured by the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV).
